overview.title: Tax, bookkeeping and consulting for individuals and small businesses.
overview.text: Everything is handled in the Greenville office by a CPA, not routed somewhere else.

services.title: Individual Tax Returns
services.summary: Federal returns for individuals and families.
services.text: Federal returns for individuals and families, prepared, reviewed and filed by a certified public accountant.
services.lead: A personal return is Form 1040, prepared, reviewed and filed by a certified public accountant in the Greenville office.
services.imageAlt: A hand signing a printed form with a fountain pen

covers.title: Taxpayer and spouse details
covers.text: The intake sheet collects the details for both filers before the first appointment.

covers.title: Dependents
covers.text: Who is claimed on the return, listed on the intake sheet.

covers.title: Direct deposit information
covers.text: Bank details for a refund, which is why the sheet is brought or faxed to the office rather than emailed.

covers.title: Contact details and addresses
covers.text: Physical and mailing addresses, cell, home and work phones and a primary email, all collected on the one sheet.

covers.title: A new child
covers.text: If you have a new child we will need a copy of their Social Security card, so bring it along with the sheet.

questions.q: What should I bring to a first appointment?
questions.a: The Individual Client Information sheet, filled in. Bring it to your first appointment and we can get straight to the work.

questions.q: Can I email the intake sheet?
questions.a: No. It asks for Social Security and bank account numbers, and ordinary email is not a safe way to send those. Bring or fax the finished sheet to the office.

services.title: Business Tax Returns
services.summary: Returns for LLCs and closely held companies.
services.text: Returns tailored to sole proprietorships, LLCs and closely held companies, with the schedules each one needs.
services.lead: An entity return turns on how the business is classified and which filings it already handles. The business intake sheet covers both before the work starts.
services.imageAlt: Hands holding printed tax forms beside a calculator and a laptop

covers.title: Corporation, S-corp, partnership or non-profit
covers.text: The return that follows from how the entity is classified: 1120 for a corporation, 1120-S for an S-corporation, 1065 for a partnership and 990 for a non-profit.

covers.title: Single member LLC or sole proprietor
covers.text: An owner-operated business is filed on a 1040 with the schedules it needs.

covers.title: Payroll, 1099 and sales tax
covers.text: Which of these filings the business already handles, so nothing is filed twice or missed.

covers.title: Prior filings and formation documents
covers.text: A business that has filed a federal return before brings a copy of that prior filing, and a newly established one brings copies of its formation documents.

questions.q: Which form do I fill in for a business?
questions.a: The New Business Client Information sheet. It covers how the business is classified and which filings it already handles.

questions.q: Do you take on new businesses outside filing season?
questions.a: Yes. New clients are welcome year-round, not just in the spring.

questions.q: Can you handle payroll and sales tax as well as the return?
questions.a: Yes. The business intake sheet has a space to request additional services alongside the return, such as bookkeeping, payroll and sales tax filings.

services.title: Bookkeeping
services.summary: Records kept current through the year.
services.text: General bookkeeping that keeps your records current through the year, so filing season is not a scramble.
services.lead: General bookkeeping kept up through the year, so the records are ready when the return is due rather than rebuilt in the spring.
services.imageAlt: A calculator and a pen resting on a page of figures

services.title: Financial Statements
services.text: Income statement preparation and period-end reporting you can hand to a bank, a partner or a buyer.
services.lead: Income statement preparation and period-end reporting, put together so it can go straight to a bank, a partner or a buyer.
services.imageAlt: A printed report of bar and pie charts beside a binder on a desk

services.title: Tax Consulting
services.summary: Planning around tax law as it shifts.
services.text: Planning around tax law as it shifts, and making sure you claim the deductions you are entitled to.
services.lead: Tax law moves, and planning around it is the difference between a return that is correct and one that is also right for you. We make sure you claim the deductions you are entitled to.

about.title: A certified public accounting firm in Greenville since 1980.
text: Rutherford Taylor & Company opened in Greenville in 1980 and has served individuals and businesses here ever since. Most of our work comes from clients who have been with us for years, and from the people they send our way.
The approach has not changed much: personal attention, accurate work, and an explanation you can actually follow. You will know who is handling your return, and you can reach them directly.

faqs.q: Can I email the new client forms?
faqs.a: No. They ask for Social Security and bank account numbers, and ordinary email is not a safe way to send those. Type into the PDF, save a copy, and bring or fax the finished sheet to the office.

faqs.q: When can I reach the office?
faqs.a: Someone answers the phone between 8am and 5pm, Monday through Friday. The office closes for lunch from noon to 1pm, and is closed Saturday and Sunday.
